children: US crude stocks rose while gasoline and distillate inventories fell last week, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday.
Crude inventories rose by 3 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels in the week ended September 18, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 641,000-barrel draw.
Crude stocks at the Cushing, Oklahoma, delivery hub (USOICC=ECI) rose by 2.2 million barrels in the week to 23.7 million barrels, the EIA said.
Oil futures were little changed following the report. Global Brent crude futures
were trading at $101.64 a barrel, up $2.39, at 10:37 a.m. ET (1437 GMT), while US West Texas Intermediate futures
Refinery crude runs (USOICR=ECI) fell by 519,000 barrels per day in the week, the EIA said, while utilization rates (USOIRU=ECI) fell by 2.8 percentage points in the week to 94%.
US gasoline stocks (USOILG=ECI) fell by 1.7 million barrels in the week to 206 million barrels, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 0.1 million-barrel build.​

Distillate stockpiles (USOILD=ECI), which include diesel and heating oil, fell by 0.4 million barrels in the week to 107.4 million barrels, versus expectations for a 0.6 million-barrel drop, the EIA data showed.
Net US crude imports (USOICI=ECI) rose last week by 369,000 barrels per day, the EIA said.
